From: Lina Park <lina@glowcode.dev>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: Quick question about GitHub app permissions + demo?

Hi Jasmine,

I signed up for Redwood last night (thanks for making the signup so smooth). I’m one of the maintainers at GlowCode OSS and started installing the GitHub app, but I hit a couple of questions before we finish the setup:

- Does the app require write permissions to repos to enable code-aware caching, or can we grant read-only scope?
- We manage ~50 repos across a single org — is org-level installation fully supported or do we need to install per-repo?
- Do you store any repository contents or only metadata (e.g., commit SHAs, file paths) for inference caching?
- We run CI on self-hosted runners — any special considerations?

Would appreciate a 20–30 min walkthrough so we can confirm the integration model and security story. Our team is US-based (PST) and next week mornings work best.

Thanks —
Lina Park
Engineering Lead, GlowCode OSS
integrations@glowcode.dev

Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 10:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Quick question about GitHub app permissions + demo?

Hi Lina — great to meet you and welcome to Redwood!

Thanks for the detailed questions — all good ones. I can cover the basics and loop in our solutions engineer for the deeper bits. A few quick answers to unblock you:

- We have a read-only permission mode for many features; a small set of more advanced caching/PR-automation features require repo write access (I can show the tradeoffs).
- Org-level install is supported and is the recommended path for teams managing many repos.
- We do not persist source code blobs in plaintext; we keep indexed metadata and optional KV caches — I’ll have Ava confirm the exact retention and encryption details.
- Self-hosted runners are supported; does your CI upload artifacts to the cloud or stay within your network?

Best,
Jasmine Liu

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick question about GitHub app permissions + demo?

Hi Lina — thanks for the context and for scheduling. Quick answers to the technical bullets (I’ll run through these in the call and share links):

- Minimum access: most inference features only need repo:contents read access and metadata (commits, PRs). Write access is optional and used for automation (e.g., automated labels or PR comments) which you can opt-out of.
- Org install: supported. When installed at org-level you can scope access to selected repositories if you prefer — install at org and then restrict to the repos we should index.
- Data handling: Redwood does not store full repository source as plaintext in our hosted offering. We persist indexed metadata and tokenized representations for caching; customers can opt into ephemeral caches and configure retention in the Console. For regulated setups we offer Private (VPC/on-prem) where code never leaves the customer network — happy to walk through both models. Our default retention is 30 days for ephemeral caches unless configured otherwise; we encrypt at rest with KMS.
- Self-hosted runners: supported. If you want to keep artifacts on-prem we can use a connector or Private deployment to avoid transferring blobs.

For the call on Wed 6/16 10:00am PST, I’ll prepare a short demo focused on: install flow (org vs repo), permission tradeoffs, and how caching works. If you send your CI owner’s email I’ll invite them and include a short technical checklist.

Agenda (proposed):
1) Quick intros (3 min)
2) Install flow & permissions (8 min)
3) Demo: repo indexing + cache behavior (10 min)
4) Q&A / next steps (9 min)

Looking forward to it —
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai
